newsitem.title: FRANCE: No tax cuts for rich -- French Socialist party chief.
newsitem.headline: No tax cuts for rich -- French Socialist party chief.

text.p: French Socialist party chief Francois Hollande said on Tuesday the new government would not enact tax cuts planned by the former government that he said favoured the wealthy.

"The tax cuts for the most favoured classes of people, no," Hollande said in an interview with RMC radio. "Today, if there are going to be tax cuts, we must go notably by way of the TVA (VAT)(Sales tax) and they must concern all the French and not only a minority of them," Hollande said.
The government of former prime minister Alain Juppe promised tax cuts of 25 billion francs in 1997, primarily through a cut in income tax.
Only about one half of French families currently pay income tax.
